ep-carrillo--pledge.description: Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's Pledge is rolled at his factory in the Dominican Republic with a U.S.-grown wrapper, an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler. Black coffee anchors the smoke from start to finish, while black cherry and licorice sweetness fade as pepper slowly builds. A dark, layered cigar for the evening.

thirds.notes: Black coffee with black cherry and licorice up front; white pepper and wood stay behind.
The pepper rises steadily while the cherry and licorice sweetness recedes.
Coffee keeps control, pepper presses close and wood grows, with fruit far in the background.

ep-carrillo--pledge-purple.description: A limited Premier Collection release that builds on Pledge with an extended-aged Havana-seed Connecticut wrapper, a Mexican binder and Nicaraguan filler from Estelí, Condega and Ometepe. Coffee and earth lead early with dark chocolate and licorice behind; later the smoke turns earthier and mineral, with white pepper on the retrohale.

thirds.notes: Coffee, dark chocolate, licorice and earth, kept distinct rather than blended into mocha.
Coffee and earth stay in front as white pepper and a mineral note appear and the chocolate fades.
Earth and mineral lead to the end, with pepper, licorice and coffee in support.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Pledge Purple Toro review

ep-carrillo--deep-blue.description: A numbered limited edition of 2026 from the Perez-Carrillo series, made in a single 6 x 56 size at Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic. A Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper covers a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler. The maker describes a smooth, sweet start, then earth and body, with spice building slowly through the smoke.

sources.title: Casa Carrillo – Deep Blue Limited Edition 2026

ep-carrillo--encore.description: The follow-up to La Historia in the Perez-Carrillo series, Encore is a Nicaraguan puro rolled in the Dominican Republic: wrapper, binder and filler are all Nicaraguan. Cedar fused with natural tobacco sweetness leads the way, a touch of fruit fades early, and earth and black pepper gain ground towards the end.

thirds.notes: Cedar and sweet natural tobacco in front, with fruit close behind and black pepper on the retrohale.
The cedar and tobacco blend turns sweet and bitter at once as the fruit fades.
Earth moves forward beside the cedar while the pepper rises a little.

ep-carrillo--encore-black.description: Encore Black gives the Encore concept a darker coat: a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over a binder from Mexico's San Andrés valley, with Nicaraguan filler from Condega, Estelí and Jalapa. Coffee leads the first half over peppercorn, earth and cedar, before a mineral earthiness takes over in the final third.

thirds.notes: Peppercorn, coffee and earth, with cedar joining; coffee soon takes the lead.
Coffee holds while the earth turns mineral and cedar grows in intensity.
The mineral earth becomes the main note, with coffee, peppercorn and cedar behind.

ep-carrillo--la-historia.description: La Historia honours Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's mother and daughter, both pictured on the band. A Mexican wrapper covers an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler, rolled in the Dominican Republic. After a short burst of pepper, earth and a syrupy mocha sweetness with a hint of black cherry carry the smoke, with pepper returning late.

thirds.notes: Black and white pepper at first, then earth and a syrupy mocha sweetness with black cherry.
Earth becomes the main note, with mocha and pepper in support.
Pepper rises close to the front without overwhelming, and mocha still surfaces at times.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – La Historia E-III review

ep-carrillo--la-historia-silk.description: La Historia Silk is the first round-format Perez-Carrillo released in the U.S., shaped by conversations with women across the cigar community. An Ecuador Habano wrapper from Quevedo, fermented and aged for 18 months, covers a Nicaraguan binder and filler from Estelí, Pennsylvania, the Dominican Republic and San Andrés. The maker describes a balanced medium smoke of earth, sweetness and spice.

ep-carrillo--allegiance.description: A collaboration between Casa Carrillo and Oliva, Allegiance is made in Nicaragua with an eighth-priming Sumatra wrapper from Quevedo, Ecuador, over a Nicaraguan binder and filler. Wood leads the smoke from start to finish, early fruit sweetness fades by the middle, and earth steadily rises to share the final third.

thirds.notes: White pepper, fruit and a damp wood that soon turns clean and moves to the front.
Wood remains in charge as the fruit recedes and earth slowly builds.
Earth joins the wood at the front, with traces of pepper and fruit behind.

ep-carrillo--endure.description: Part of the Perez-Carrillo series, Endure is built around a Meerapfel Cameroon wrapper and honours the Meerapfel family's work to keep that leaf in cultivation. The binder and filler are Nicaraguan, and the cigar is rolled in the Dominican Republic. The maker describes a medium smoke with Cameroon spice over smooth undertones.

thirds.notes: Toasty caramel with a light saltiness and a pretzel-like note over rich earth.
Creamy and sweet, with cashew and Brazil nut, aged oak and a maple-candy touch.
Creamy caramel and smoky oak with café au lait and a bright, cherry-like fruit.

ep-carrillo--ascend.description: A regular-production addition to the Perez-Carrillo series, Ascend wraps an Ecuador Habano leaf around an Estelí binder and Nicaraguan filler, rolled in the Dominican Republic. It was blended around gradual progression, so the smoke is meant to change slowly from the first draw to the last. Its three sizes are named Saddle, Ridge and Peak.

ep-carrillo--essence-sumatra.description: The first blend in the Essence Series, which focuses on the role of the wrapper. An Ecuador Sumatra leaf covers a double binder of Nicaraguan and Honduran tobacco, with Nicaraguan and Dominican filler, made at Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic. The maker lists almond, coffee, white pepper and raw sugar in a medium smoke.

sources.title: Casas Fumando – E.P. Carrillo Essence Sumatra review

thirds.notes: A quick flash of black pepper, then raisin, dark chocolate and a woody, musky earth.
Raisin sweetness and deep wood lead, with lighter chocolate and a berry note.
Wood and musk move ahead of the raisin, with a piney aftertaste and a light nicotine touch.

ep-carrillo--essence-maduro.description: The Maduro in the Essence Series pairs a Mexican San Andrés wrapper with a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler. Mocha opens the smoke and separates into chocolate and an increasingly bitter coffee, while pepper climbs to share the lead in the final third. A dark, everyday smoke for after dinner.

thirds.notes: Mocha leads over cedar, earth and white pepper, with mixed pepper on the retrohale.
Chocolate and coffee separate, the coffee turning more bitter past the midpoint.
Coffee and pepper share the front, with cedar and earth in the background.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Essence Maduro Robusto review

ep-carrillo--essence-honduras.description: A collaboration with Plasencia, the Honduras blend of the Essence Series uses an Olancho San Agustín wrapper and a Honduran binder, with Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Fruit and earth open, coffee soon takes over, and pepper grows through the second half. The maker also lists dark chocolate and oak.

thirds.notes: Fruit in front with earth and coffee behind, and mixed pepper on the tongue and retrohale.
Coffee becomes the main note while fruit and earth settle into the background.
Coffee still leads and pepper keeps rising to become the main supporting note.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Essence Honduras Toro review

ep-carrillo--essence-connecticut.description: The fourth Essence blend is made at the DIADEMA factory in Honduras rather than at Casa Carrillo. An Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper covers a Honduran Criollo 98 binder with Honduran and Dominican filler. The maker describes a mild, creamy smoke with hay, light pepper, toasted almond and cedar, suited to a quiet morning.

ep-carrillo--inch-natural.description: The INCH Series is built around large ring gauges, from 60 upward. The Natural uses an Ecuadorian wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder, with Nicaraguan and Dominican filler, rolled in the Dominican Republic. It smokes medium, led by sweet cedar and floral notes, with coffee and nuts behind and a light red pepper.

ep-carrillo--inch-maduro.description: The maduro member of the large-ring INCH Series uses a U.S.-grown wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder, with Nicaraguan and Dominican filler, rolled in the Dominican Republic. The maker rates it medium to full, a step up in strength from the INCH Natural.

ep-carrillo--inch-nicaragua.description: Made in Nicaragua, the INCH Nicaragua is a Nicaraguan puro in the large-ring INCH Series. Earth and baker's spice open, natural tobacco sweetness and wood carry the middle as pepper grows, and the body builds from medium to medium-full along the way.

thirds.notes: Earth and baker's spice lead, with cedar, wood and black pepper behind.
Sweet natural tobacco and spice hold the front while pepper increases on tongue and retrohale.
Wood follows the natural tobacco, with spice, cedar, pepper and earth rounding it out.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – INCH Nicaragua No. 60 review

ep-carrillo--new-wave-connecticut.description: Perez-Carrillo's take on a Connecticut cigar: an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled in the Dominican Republic. It is mild in strength but full of flavour, opening with butter and cream and a berry-like sweetness, then moving to wood and cedar spice, with a little coffee near the end.

thirds.notes: Buttery cream right away, soon joined by a sweetness that recalls strawberries.
Wood emerges after the first third, and cedar spice grows as the cream and fruit recede.
The spice increases in the last third, with hints of coffee in the background.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – New Wave Connecticut review
